newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian PM appeals to West as crisis deepens.
newsitem.headline: Albanian PM appeals to West as crisis deepens.

text.p: Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino appealed directly to Western governments on Tuesday to help solve a political crisis he warned could have "unforeseen consequences" for his violence-ravaged nation.
Italy and Greece, reflecting widespread Western concern, stepped up appeals to Albania's political parties to strike a deal on free and fair elections.

Despite marathon talks on Monday, Fino failed once again to persuade most political parties of his national unity government to take part in June 29 elections seen as vital to prevent a new upsurge of unrest in the Balkan state.

"Although the debate continued all Monday, it failed not only to bring compromise or come near to compromise, but on the contrary took Albania to the edge of a deeper crisis with unforeseen consequences," Fino's office said in a statement.
The parties are in dispute over an electoral law which most of them say is unfairly biased towards President Sali Berisha and his former ruling Democratic Party.

"I told the parties I would not discuss with them any more but I will address international public opinion," said Fino, who spoke late on Monday with Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, European envoy Franz Vranitzky and U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum.
Former Stalinist Albania plunged into anarchy and violence in February and March after thousands of people were left penniless by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.
Violence has subsided in recent weeks but some regions remain lawless. Nine people have been reported killed in gunfire since Sunday.
Italy, leading a multinational force protecting humanitarian aid, called again for political compromise.
"The next 24 hours are very important for the future of Albania," Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta told reporters in Rome.
Prime Minister Prodi said he would work to the "last hours" to make sure elections go ahead.

Greece said failure to reach an election compromise would jeopardise the continued presence of the 6,000-strong eight-nation troop force. Western countries have already warned they may cut aid to Albania unless elections go ahead.
As Fino continued his efforts, Berisha was once more campaigning for an election that may not take place.
"I invite all Albanians to turn this vote into the freest and most honest campaign that we have known," he told supporters in Fier, some 110 km (70 miles) south of the capital, Tirana.

Genc Pollo, a senior Democratic Party official, said the parties still disagreed over how many seats should be decided by proportional representation and how many by first-past-the-post majority voting.

The right-wing Democratic Party and its main rival, the Socialists, have been clashing for months over electoral rules. The Democrats favour more majority voting while the Socialists back more proportional representation.
In a separate incident, Greece's foreign ministry said the head bodyguard at its consulate in the southern town of Gjirokaster killed himself accidentally on Tuesday while cleaning his gun.
